summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, diabetes, and recent hernia repair was readmitted after a blood culture from a prior discharge grew gram-negative rods. He was asymptomatic but started on intravenous cefepime. Imaging with CT and MRI revealed findings suggestive of possible cholangitis related to biliary stents, which were removed via ERCP. A PICC line was placed for two weeks of outpatient antibiotic therapy. His kidney function improved during the stay, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue sirolimus and Myfortic, stop Lasix and fenofibrate pending primary care review, and follow up for transplant care and pancreatic cyst monitoring.
problems: Other specified bacterial infections in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, other gram-negative organisms
